newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside sees softer Japan LNG demand.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside sees softer Japan LNG demand.

text.p: Australia's Woodside Petroleum Ltd on Wednesday forecast softer demand for its main product, liquefied natural gas (LNG), from Japanese customers this year.
Woodside managing director John Akehurst said Japanese buyers of LNG from the Woodside-operated North-West Shelf gas fields had sought a reduction in cargoes for calendar 1997.
Japanese cusotmers will take 125 cargoes under contract this year, down from 130 in 1996, he told a news conference after Woodside reported a 58 percent surge in 1996 net earnings.
"We will be looking to sell those cargoes on the spot market and we have contracted or chartered an additional LNG ship to permit us to take the opportunity to do that," Akehurst said.
He blamed the slackening in Japanese demand on a short-term increase in supply into that market.
Woodside owns a sixth share of the North West Shelf fields.

Its equal partners are units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp and the Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
